subject: Archaeology
title: AI Reading Ancient Texts
description: A tiny lesson with a big payoff: AI Reading Ancient Texts.

hook.text: A machine-learning model trained on Greek can fill in missing text on broken inscriptions.

buildup.text: DeepMind's Ithaca model was trained on 78,000 ancient Greek inscriptions to predict gaps.

discovery.text: Ithaca scored 62 percent accuracy. Human experts alone managed just 25 percent.

twist.text: AI does not replace scholars. When humans used Ithaca's tips, accuracy jumped to 72 percent.

climax.text: Similar AI is now being trained for cuneiform and Egyptian hieratic. Millions of texts await.

punchline.text: A computer reads broken Greek better than experts. Together they read best.

quiz.question: How does AI help with ancient inscription analysis?
options: It replaces human scholars entirely with automated translations
It predicts missing text, and when combined with humans, boosts accuracy to 72%
It photographs inscriptions and uploads them for crowdsourcing

details.summary: Artificial intelligence is deciphering damaged ancient texts that human scholars cannot read. Machine learning models trained on known scripts reconstruct missing letters in broken tablets and scrolls, most notably reading carbonized Herculaneum papyri and fragmentary cuneiform tablets.
details.whyItMatters: Thousands of ancient texts remain unread due to damage. AI can process fragments far faster than humans and detect patterns invisible to the eye, potentially unlocking lost literature, laws, and scientific knowledge from antiquity.
takeaways: AI reconstructs missing text in damaged ancient documents
Machine learning reads carbonized scrolls from Herculaneum
It processes thousands of fragments faster than human scholars

faq.question: How does AI read burned Herculaneum scrolls?
faq.answer: X-ray tomography captures internal structure of rolled carbonized papyri without unrolling them. AI algorithms detect subtle density differences between ink and papyrus, then reconstruct the text layer by layer. The Vesuvius Challenge has used this approach to read previously illegible scrolls.

faq.question: Can AI decipher completely unknown scripts?
faq.answer: Not yet. AI works best when trained on known examples of a script. For undeciphered writing like Linear A or the Indus script, AI can identify patterns and statistical properties but cannot assign meaning without some bilingual reference point.
